sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 22 = check 21; Internal Quality Checks row 22)
evidence: Source review against the eight-step test.sh contract in staged-task-contract.md; every step holds. tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the frozen template (both sha256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa), LF-only, and `bash -n` succeeds; tests/tools/score.py, tests/Dockerfile and environment/Dockerfile are also identical to the template, and task.toml differs from it only in identity/metadata fields. (1) Reward on every path: test.sh:60 `write_zero_reward` then :61 `trap cleanup EXIT`, and cleanup ends in `ensure_reward` (test.sh:33-40), both before the first early exit at :63; the zero record (test.sh:8) carries reward, the five dimensions, gates_passed, floors_passed, weighted_score, graded and no_op. Because the zero is on disk before anything else, a `set -e` abort (for example the {app_context} substitution at :195-201) or an external kill still leaves a reward. No `exec` builtin is used (only `find -exec` at :86). (2) Refusal paths exit 0 with the zero record: missing judge env :63-66, missing /app/server.js :68-70, symlink escaping /app/node_modules :72-83. (3) Safe launch: /app copied to /tmp/submission (:90-95); app started with `setsid env -i` carrying only PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT, DB_PATH and `setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups` (:104-111); /tests is made unreadable to that uid (`chmod -R go-rwx /tests` :12, umask 077, LOG_DIR 700), so the submission cannot read the rubric or write the reward. (4) Liveness: probe of /api/health then / for up to 120 x 0.25 s (:115-122), `exit 0` if not ready (:123-125), before any rewardkit call. (5) Restart helper generated by heredoc plus sed, chmod 755, `export APP_RESTART_HELPER` (:127-193), referenced by scored/functional/judge.toml `args = ["/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py", "$APP_RESTART_HELPER"]`; cleanup re-reads app.pid so a restarted process is also killed. (6) Order and scoring: `run_suite gates 1500` (:213) then `python3 /tests/tools/score.py "$LOG_DIR"` (:217) with 0 continue / 1 `exit 0` keeping the detailed record / other `write_zero_reward; exit 0` (:218-222); then `run_suite scored 11100` (:224) and `score.py ... || write_zero_reward` (:227). score.py returns 1 only for a real gate failure and 2 on any exception (score.py:83-91), matching those branches. A scored-suite timeout or crash leaves the post-gates record, whose reward is 0.0 because floors_passed requires scored data (score.py:42-48), so no partial run can leak a positive reward. (7) Budgets nest: gate judges 600+600=1200 < 1500; scored judges 9000+900+900=10800 < 11100 (run serially by --max-concurrent-agent 1); 1500+11100=12600 < [verifier].timeout_sec 13200. Run evidence (earlier candidate only, hashes verified on LF-normalised bytes): Oracle verifier/reward.json shows the full path writing `"reward": 0.9833 ... "graded": 1` (sha bcfe3714...), and the model trial shows the gate-failure path writing `"render": 0.0 ... "reward": 0.0, "gates_passed": 0, "graded": 1` with no scored directory, i.e. both main branches produced a reward. Scripted golden run on these bytes (run_golden.sh sha a94328b9..., verified) launches with the same uid/env -i line but does not go through tests/test.sh. Risk is true only because tests/test.sh has not been executed in the verifier image on these exact task bytes; the unreached refusal branches (missing server.js, symlink escape, liveness timeout, score.py exit 2) are verified by reading, not by a run. Weak-app probes considered: an app that never listens, one that ships a symlink out of /app, one that crashes after the gates, and one that hangs the scored judge all end at reward 0.0 with files present; a conforming app that keeps its database beside server.js and honours DB_PATH launches either from /app or from the copy. No defect found.
